type_reason: New method that adds a galaxy-catalog prior to Bilby parameter estimation, benchmarked on three public events and own simulated BNS injections.
headline: Galaxy-catalog prior recovers the GW170817 host as most probable galaxy after mass reweighting with smaller area and volume, but gives no improvement over a simple catalog crossmatch on simulated BNS.

F1.scope: Searched abstract, Sec 3.1-3.4 for the reference behind the performance claims.
F1.note: Simulated-BNS result is against own injections in Gaussian noise (Sec 3.4) and against a crossmatch built from the same posteriors. This is standard practice for a method benchmark and the headline for simulations is a null. GW170817 reference is the EM-identified host, a separate source.

F2.quote: 131 events pass this S/N cut, of which ten events were removed due to problems with sky map generation from posterior samples (for either the 2D or 3D localizations), resulting in 121 simulated BNS
F2.scope: Searched abstract and Sec 3.4 for a best case or a selected subset.
F2.note: Simulated sample is reported as a full cumulative distribution with the event count and the removed events disclosed. Real-event results are three named events, not a pick of best.

F3.scope: Searched abstract and Sec 3 for a claim with no interval.
F3.note: Abstract says significantly decreased area and volume. Table 1 gives single-run 90% area and volume with no interval. This is a comparison of localisation sizes, not a detection or deviation claim, so SCOPE.

F4.quote: utilizing a version of Bilby with an additional prior class
F4.scope: Searched whole text for links, data or code availability statements.
F4.note: No link or availability statement found. The modified Bilby with a galaxy prior class, the posteriors and the 121 simulated-event outputs are not linked. Software list names only public packages. Bones to confirm against the journal page.

F5.quote: we acknowledge that this could result in a ≈ 8% bias in our cumulative results
F5.scope: Recomputed counts and Table 2 products from printed numbers.
F5.note: 131 - 10 = 121 simulated events (printed 121). 10/131 = 7.6 percent (printed approx 8 percent). Table 2 NGC 4993: 1.06e-1 x 5.05e-2 = 5.35e-3 (printed 5.36e-3, within rounding of the 3-digit inputs); ESO 575-G023: 1.47e-2 x 3.03e-1 = 4.45e-3 (printed 4.44e-3, same).

F6.quote: Our list places NGC 4993 second (10.7% probability)
F6.scope: Compared abstract and prose numbers with Tables 1-2 and figure captions for GW170817.
F6.note: Text gives NGC 4993 posterior probability as 10.7 percent, while Table 2 lists f_posterior for NGC 4993 as 1.06 x 10^-1 (10.6 percent). Table 2 caption: f_posterior is the fraction of total posterior support from the catalog-informed localization alone. Difference is in the last digit, so it may be rounding or a different run. Bones to decide. Abstract claims (most probable after mass reweighting, rank 1 in Table 2) and Table 1 area and volume agree with the text.

F7.scope: Searched Sec 3.4 and the abstract for a matched baseline with an interval.
F7.note: Paper itself reports that the simple crossmatch of the catalog with the initial localization, sorted by volume probability, performs similarly to the method with a 3D catalog (Sec 3.4, p.9). No interval or matched margin printed, so no read.

F2.scope: Searched abstract and Sec 3.2 for a best case.

F3.scope: Searched Sec 3.1 and 3.2 for claims with no interval.
